references.text: Judas kisses Jesus as a sign to betray him, and Jesus is arrested, which resembles how Jesus is seized in Mark.
Jesus is arrested in the Garden of Gethsemane, parallel to the event in Mark.
Jesus is arrested by a group of soldiers and servants from the chief priests and Pharisees, referring to a similar arrest as in Mark.
The prophecy that the Messiah would suffer silently and not open his mouth during persecution, which can be seen as a foreshadowing of Jesus' arrest.
